entities.summary: Franz Josef Rudigier was an Austrian Roman Catholic prelate and served as the Bishop of Linz from his appointment in 1853 until his death. Much of his local diocese grew due to his vigorous in promoting evangelic zeal and fundamental religious principles. He became the intellectual figurehead for Catholics in their struggle with liberalism. He promoted the Christian press and took a visible stand defending the 1855 concordat, when liberals annulled it without papal consultation in 1870. A beatification process for Rudigier was initiated under Pope Pius X in 1905 and he was titled as a Servant of God.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Rudigier's promotion of evangelic zeal and fundamental religious principles contributed to the growth of his local diocese, while his defense of the 1855 concordat had significant consequences for Catholicism in Austria. His beatification process initiated under Pope Pius X reflects his lasting impact on the Catholic Church.
